descriptionNullable:
This dataset contains ophthalmic, demographic, and lifestyle measurements from undergraduate medical students.

The purpose of the dataset is to model different forms of myopia and classify students into several diagnostic categories.


Training Features (X_train.csv)

This file contains the input features used to train the models.
It includes:
	•	Demographic information:
age, sex, height, weight, BMI, etc.
	•	Refractive and ocular measurements:
axial length (LA), spherical equivalent (SE), keratometry, corneal curvature, CUVAF metrics, anterior chamber depth, IOP, etc.
	•	Lifestyle variables:
hours of near work, outdoor exposure, screen time, sleep patterns, physical activity, etc.
	•	Family history and medical background:
parental myopia, familiar myopia number, genetic predisposition, etc.

All variables are anonymized and numerical/categorical.


Training Labels (Y_train.csv)

This file contains the target labels corresponding to each student in the training set.
It includes four different diagnostic outputs:
	•	M → Presence of myopia (YES/NO)
	•	MM → Presence of high myopia / myopia magna (YES/NO)
	•	Combo → Combined label:
	•	C (control),
	•	M (myopia),
	•	MM (myopia magna)
	•	DCombo → Extended classification:
	•	C (control)
	•	M1 / M2 (myopia subtypes)
	•	MM (myopia magna)

These labels are used to train both binary and multiclass learning models.


Test Features (X_test.csv)

This file contains the unlabeled test samples for which predictions are required.
It follows the same structure and preprocessing as X_train.csv, except for the missing target columns.

The goal is to generate predictions for:
	•	M
	•	MM
	•	Combo
	•	DCombo

for each student in this test set.
